items.title: Michael Max Fleming interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017
items.q: And I began to play with Eddie “Cleanhead” Vincent.

ctx.x: I was playing with him at 17, that summer. That’s before this time when I’m making this decision. I’m at home on a Sunday afternoon and the phone rings. It’s my uncle calling

my mother Bec, her name was Rebecca. “Bec, the bass player didn’t show up, can you sent Michael over?” to what was Newport, Kentucky, which was the Las Vegas, Sin City of the world. Everything went on over there. And you know what my mother said to him? “Are you out of your mind? Send my baby over there with those cut-throats?” Silence on the phone. But she had to back off. Because the year before that I turned professional doo-wopper and she said I couldn’t go. And she found my clothes in the hallway and she…
Oh no kidding? Wow. So you were playing a mix of jazz and blues?
